Now feature finish-per-window, one foundry_key label per call, row recorded by N31a-55.

Two contradictory key forms (fo-<step> and one derived from script, step and fixture digest, the rejected design) would give the repeated calls of steps 3 and 4 one key; the gate row was said to be written by a script and recorded by this bead's standing condition. The guard-removed builds were nc-<nnnn> features with no record behind them, so nobody could build them by name; CX-340's plant id was missing; acceptance handed the receipt to N31b-18 (a dependent). Now features named by the defect, plant id BD-406:quadratic-at-zero, row recorded by N31a-56.

KA-747's control was 'halving the offset halves the slack', which N31-KA does not register (2,063 mm and 0.628 mm unit mutations); CX-341's plant was an nc-<nnnn> feature; keys were derived from (script, step, input digest), the rejected form that collides across step 3's kill runs; acceptance required NS-20 and the KILL-PACKET hand-off, both dependents.

Registration had this bead write a record for every plant with an owner field the schema lacks and no gate: the assemble-peaks plant would be registered twice beside CX-336's seeded record, and the INV-FOUNDRY-06/-07 records would be refused no-gate. Now: reuse CX-336's record (dep N31-CX added), six INV-seeded records with their gates, two test-level controls; nine plants, not seven; no last_seen written here; e2e_key for the export key.

The script described foundry_key as derived from script, step and input digest, the form STD-E2E rejects; an implementer following it would build a colliding key helper. Now foundry_key is e2e_key under the cluster name, and the script sources the preamble library that defines it.

KA-754's controls omitted the third control N31-KA registers (ratio 2 gives 1.333); acceptance had this bead submit proposals and mark registry rows not gate-eligible, though rows are N31-KA's (a dependent) and eligibility is computed by N38a-12, so the criterion could not pass; an interim 'until the registry owner accepts them' stood in Considerations.

Section 1 told the implementer to write known_answers.toml records with fields (site, controls, gate) that differ from N38a-12's schema and duplicate N31-KA's rows, and acceptance expected rows 'awaiting registration' though N31-KA registers every tolerance and control; script keys were literals instead of e2e_key. Now the battery reads N31-KA's rows, writes their fixtures and expects all thirteen eligible.

Convention 11 flags a bead without a scripts/e2e script unless its test plan says it delivers nothing a frob command can reach; the pilot never said so, so an implementer could add a product e2e script for an experiment that has no product surface. The test plan now states it, and that the registered pilot script is its end-to-end script.

Keys were s2-<k>-<step>-<d> with d a digest of the inputs, the derived form STD-E2E rejects, and the text claimed a re-run 'resumes', which cannot happen because every script run has its own state root; now e2e_key labels per call (sim and edit per iteration, the noise-floor repeat and the resampling control apart). Also the convention-11 statement that the pilot has no scripts/e2e script.
Convention-11 statement missing: the test plan now says the pilot delivers nothing a frob command can reach and its pilot script is its end-to-end script.

The script described foundry_key as digesting registration hash, address set and stack lock so that a re-run 'resumes a pair': that is the derived key STD-E2E rejects, and with one state root per run nothing resumes, so an implementer following it would build a colliding helper. The fallback run's key was said to be derived from step and input digest (rejected form); and the --offline option was 'requested of' BD-403 and VERBS-foundry, a convention-13 request. The fired-branch keys were said to be derived from step and input digest, the form STD-E2E rejects; now foundry_key labels with the state-root reason.
Acceptance ran `frob foundry export --json` with no design, no --packet and no --key: as written it is refused (805) and cannot show the reduced packet. Now the full form of the row.

`frob eval run quad-ref --variants <set>` gave eval.run no population (VERBS-eval requires exactly one of battery or task), so the batch step would be refused with 802; keys were described as digest-derived; the decision entry omitted N40-03's `receipts` field and the gate row was said to be written by N31a-59. Now --battery smoke, foundry_key labels, receipts, row recorded from N31a-59's receipt.

Request from F-U31a-2 applied: the script described foundry_key as derived from step and input digest so that a changed catalogue gets a new key; foundry_key is e2e_key <label>, so the claim was false and steps that rely on it would replay a stored receipt. Now one label per call and no reliance on content changing the key.

Same request: foundry_key was said to digest the call's inputs, card included; and the fourth call (assumed curve under --strict-data) carried no key at all, so it would be refused 805 instead of 113. Now four labels ffa-1 to ffa-4.

Audit note applied after checking: acceptance required the GATE-FOUNDRY-12 row to state card provenance, but that row is recorded from N31a-59, which depends on this bead (convention 7); the three-call lifecycle script was the only reason for dep N31a-50, and N31a-59 step 9 already asserts 113 and 831 through the verb. The script and the gate-row item move to N31a-59 (its slice carries the matching note); dep N31a-50 dropped; unit tests on N31a-48 kept; the test plan says the bead has no frob-reachable surface of its own.

Acceptance requires every certificate and refusal to record the budget and effort in every option, but scope added the recorded budget only under options B or C and N31a-45 does not record it, so under the default option A the criterion could not pass. Scope now adds the record in every option.

Keys were described as digesting the frozen binary's identity (rejected derived form) and one pattern g13-<brief>-<step> covered 200 planted copies and the imports, which would collide; now one foundry_key label per call for checks, planted copies and imports.
